title: Could not mmap and subsequent crash on simple query, more frequently with CTEs
body:
### To reproduce

1. Run a query:
```sql
SELECT
  SUM(column_a) AS alias_a,
  SUM(column_b) AS alias_b,
  SUM(column_b):<nick> / SUM(column_a) AS alias_c,
  SUM(column_b):<nick> / 30.2 AS alias_d,
  1 - (
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN column_c <= 29 THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ):<nick> / DATEDIFF('h', '2024-08-01T07:00:00.000Z', '2024-08-15T07:00:00.000Z')
  ) AS alias_e,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN column_c <= 29 THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS alias_f
FROM table_name
WHERE
  timestamp >= '2024-08-01T07:00:00.000Z'
  AND timestamp < '2024-08-15T07:00:00.000Z'
  AND type = 'SITE';
;
```
With the above query, QuestDB will crash some of the time (I had to revise the below query with CTEs because QuestDB seemed to never be able to handle a query with multiple CTEs). However, with the below query with CTEs, we get a guaranteed crash:

```sql
WITH daily_energy AS (
  SELECT 
    timestamp,
    SUM(columnA) AS columnA,
    SUM(columnB) AS columnB,
    SUM(columnB):<nick> / 303261235.2 AS columnC
  FROM table__name_ems__hourly
  WHERE
    id = 'Site'
    AND category = 'BASE'
  SAMPLE BY 1d 
    FROM dateadd('y', -1, '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000') 
    TO '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000' 
    FILL(NULL)
  ALIGN TO CALENDAR TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'
  ORDER BY timestamp ASC
),
daily_availability AS (
  SELECT 
    timestamp,
    COALESCE(COUNT(id), 0) AS columnD
  FROM table__name_ems__hourly
  WHERE
    id = 'Site'
    AND category = 'BASE'
    AND columnE <= 29
  SAMPLE BY 1d 
    FROM dateadd('y', -1, '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000') 
    TO '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000' 
    FILL(NULL)
  ALIGN TO CALENDAR TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'
  ORDER BY timestamp ASC
),
date_range_energy AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(columnA) AS range__columnA,
    SUM(columnB) AS range__columnB,
    SUM(columnB):<nick> / 303261235.2 AS range__columnC,
    SUM(columnB) / SUM(columnA):<nick> AS range__columnD
  FROM daily_energy
  WHERE
    timestamp BETWEEN '2024-08-21T00:00:00.000000' AND '2024-08-25T23:59:59.000000'
),
date_range_availability AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(columnD) AS range__columnE,
    1 - (SUM(columnD) / datediff('h', '2024-08-21T00:00:00.000000', '2024-08-26T00:00:00.000000'):<nick>) AS range__columnF
  FROM daily_availability
  WHERE
    timestamp BETWEEN '2024-08-21T00:00:00.000000' AND '2024-08-25T23:59:59.000000'
),
mtd_energy AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(columnA) AS mtd__columnA,
    SUM(columnB) AS mtd__columnB,
    SUM(columnB):<nick> / 303261235.2 AS mtd__columnC,
    SUM(columnB) / SUM(columnA):<nick> AS mtd__columnD
  FROM daily_energy
  WHERE
    timestamp BETWEEN dateadd('M', -1, '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000') AND '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'
),
mtd_availability AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(columnD) AS mtd__columnE,
    1 - (SUM(columnD) / datediff('h', dateadd('M', -1, '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'), '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'):<nick>) AS mtd__columnF
  FROM daily_availability
  WHERE
    timestamp BETWEEN dateadd('M', -1, '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000') AND '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'
),
ytd_energy AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(columnA) AS ytd__columnA,
    SUM(columnB) AS ytd__columnB,
    SUM(columnB):<nick> / 303261235.2 AS ytd__columnC,
    SUM(columnB) / SUM(columnA):<nick> AS ytd__columnD
  FROM daily_energy
  WHERE
    timestamp BETWEEN date_trunc('year', '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000') AND '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'
),
ytd_availability AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(columnD) AS ytd__columnE,
    1 - (SUM(columnD) / datediff('h', date_trunc('year', '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'), '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'):<nick>) AS ytd__columnF
  FROM daily_availability
  WHERE
    timestamp BETWEEN date_trunc('year', '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000') AND '2024-08-31T23:59:59.000000'
),
ytd_trend_365d AS (
  SELECT 
    to_timezone(timestamp, 'America/Los_Angeles') AS timestamp,
    SUM(columnA) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '365' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ytd_sum__columnA,
    SUM(columnB) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '365' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ytd_sum__columnB,
    AVG(columnA) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '365' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ytd_avg__columnA,
    AVG(columnB) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '365' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ytd_avg__columnB,
    AVG(columnC) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '365' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ytd_avg__columnC
  FROM daily_energy
  ORDER BY timestamp DESC
  LIMIT 1
),
ytd_trend_15d AS (
  SELECT
    to_timezone(timestamp, 'America/Los_Angeles') AS timestamp,
    SUM(columnA) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '15' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ms_15d__columnA,
    SUM(columnB) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '15' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ms_15d__columnB,
    AVG(columnA) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '15' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ma_15d__columnA,
    AVG(columnB) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '15' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ma_15d__columnB,
    AVG(columnC) OVER (
      ORDER BY timestamp ASC
      RANGE BETWEEN '15' DAY PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS ma_15d__columnC
  FROM daily_energy
  ORDER BY timestamp DESC
  LIMIT 1
)

SELECT
  ytd_trend_365d.timestamp,
  date_range_energy.range__columnA,
  mtd_energy.mtd__columnA,
  ytd_energy.ytd__columnA
FROM ytd_trend_365d
CROSS JOIN ytd_energy
CROSS JOIN date_range_energy
CROSS JOIN mtd_energy
;
```

2. Observe error `could not mmap  [size=1355328, offset=0, fd=4501795742419913, memUsed=1387729134912, fileLen=1355776]`, followed by the next query causing QuestDB to crash and restart.

### QuestDB version:

8.1.4

### OS, in case of Docker specify Docker and the Host OS:

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)
Default helm chart (https://artifacthub.io/packages/helm/questdb/questdb)

### File System, in case of Docker specify Host File System:

Amazon EBS disk gp3 

### Full Name:

Peter Klingelhofer

### Affiliation:

Energy Vault

### Have you followed Linux, MacOs kernel configuration steps to increase Maximum open files and Maximum virtual memory areas limit?

- [X] Yes, I have

### Additional context

All columns being queried are DOUBLE in the schema. 

We also occasionally see this error as well:
`Error: could not open read-only [file=/var/lib/questdb/db/table__name_ems__hourly~8/2024-10-18.40666/hvac_temperature_status__mixed_air__c__mean.d.393]`
`Error: [24]: could not open read-write with clean allocation [file=/var/lib/questdb/db/table__name_ems__hourly~8/_txn_scoreboard] undefined`

If you can please include full error log line, it includes OS errno, which is missing from your report.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi @participant1, thank you for your response. There is no OS errno in the error that is outputted. This is always the error I see, with no errno: `could not mmap  [size=1361328, offset=0, fd=4501469481859109, memUsed=1426245430260, fileLen=1363968]`:

QuestDB will error, and then the next query will crash it completely, seems like Java heap is running out of memory? I've attached the fatal error and log file above in the issue description. Thank you.

EDIT:
We do occasionally see these errors too:
```
Error: could not open read-only [file=/var/lib/questdb/db/table__name_ems__hourly~8/2024-10-18.40666/hvac_temperature_status__mixed_air__c__mean.d.393]
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: hi Peter, thank you for the logs. We will try to repro asap. From the crash log you attached it looks like the crash originated in the "writer" process. It is possible that read and write are somehow connected, although not likely. I will keep you updated. Are you on slack by any chance?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Thanks so much. And yes, I'm on QuestDB's Slack, I just sent you a direct message.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: It seems that doing multiple queries at once via `Promise.all` in TypeScript causes this, when we loop over each query and linearly await the response we don't see the above behavior as often. This was surprising because it seems that typically QuestDB supports high concurrency quite well.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I just attempted CTEs without the `Promise.all` (so running multiple queries in serial, waiting on the previous one to complete), and I'm still seeing `could not open read-only [file=/var/lib/questdb/db/table__name__hourly~8/2024-08-07.35302/aux_current_status__ac_current__a__ma.d.206` errors, so it seems that the `Promise.all` / parallel concurrency vs in serial wasn't the direct cause of the problem after all.

All of this could be happening due to insufficient mmap area kernel limit. Have you followed this doc section on your server machine? https://questdb.com/docs/deployment/capacity-planning/#os-configuration

```

2025-01-16T19:57:48.588942Z A server-main vm.max_map_count checked [limit=1048576]
```
